notes: Solved independently first. At constant pressure Q = nC_pΔT and ΔU = nC_vΔT, so ΔU = Q(C_v/C_p) = Q/γ for each gas with the same Q. Monatomic γ = 5/3 gives ΔU₁ = 3Q/5; diatomic γ = 7/5 gives ΔU₂ = 5Q/7; the ratio is (3/5)(7/5) = 21/25, option 3. Confirmed exactly in python (sympy Rational). Every printed equation follows from the one above it, and the why_this_step on step 0 (only part of the heat raises internal energy at constant pressure, the rest does expansion work) is the correct reason for that line. The single common_mistakes entry is true: treating the process as if it were at constant volume makes ΔU = Q for both gases and gives 1:1, which is the option-4 value. mistake_type_hint concept fits. Considered and did not file: difficulty is marked hard, which reads a little high for a one-formula result, but it is not clearly off since the ΔU = Q/γ step is the non-obvious part and the distractors 9:49 and 3:7 are built from plausible wrong ratios; also, only one of the three wrong options carries a mistake entry, which is thin coverage but not an error.
